title: Cosine feature ledger with a matched divisor
summary: Address and probe vectors are mapped through a fixed bank of cosine features. Each symbol adds the product of its address features and its content to a ledger and adds the features alone to a divisor vector. The read takes the probe's features against the ledger and divides by the same features against the divisor.
core_idea: Approximate an exponential similarity read with fixed cosine features so the whole history fits in a ledger of feature-content products and a feature tally.

state.name: G
state.meaning: Ledger of summed feature-content products, m cosine features by d content coordinates.

state.name: r
state.meaning: Divisor: summed cosine features of every earlier address.

state.name: Omega
state.meaning: Frequencies of the cosine features, drawn once at random from a standard normal and never trained.

update.name: features
update.latex: \psi(v) = \sqrt{2/m}\, \cos(\Omega v + \omega_0),\; f_t = \psi(W_a e_t),\; c_t = W_c e_t
update.plain: psi(v) = sqrt(2/m) cos(Omega v + omega_0) with fixed phases omega_0; f_t = psi(W_a e_t), content c_t = W_c e_t

update.name: ledger
update.plain: G_t = G_(t-1) + outer(f_t, c_t); r_t = r_(t-1) + f_t

readout.name: read
readout.plain: g_t = psi(W_b e_t); y_t = G_t^T g_t / (r_t . g_t), the normalized read; next symbol scores O y_t

learning.description: Every matrix and offset is learned by gradient descent on the cross-entropy of the next symbol over a training corpus, with backpropagation through the whole sequence. The frequencies Omega and phases omega_0 stay fixed.
learning.few_shot_argument: No structure for few examples; about 3500 training sequences are needed for recall of 4 pairs.

complexity.total_sequence: Theta(n m d + n d V)
complexity.constants_notes: m cosines, one rank-one write and one m by d read per symbol; ledger and divisor are m d + m numbers.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Gradient descent with no structure for few examples.

prediction.statement: From random weights, 3500 training sequences of 4 pairs over 16 symbols give recall accuracy 0.99.

capabilities.prediction: Approximate recall whose error shrinks as m grows; exact only when the K address features are orthogonal, which needs K <= m.
For unit-norm addresses the expected read equals the exponential-similarity weighted mean of contents, with variance of order 1/m.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: Recall error does not decrease when m is raised from 64 to 1024 at K = 16.
The counted operations grow faster than linearly in n at fixed m, d and V.

toy_example.description: Two writes with m = 2 fixed cosine features and one read.
toy_example.python:
import json, math
Om = [[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]]
ph = [0.3, -0.2]
def psi(v):
    return [math.sqrt(1.0) * math.cos(Om[i][0] * v[0] + Om[i][1] * v[1] + ph[i]) for i in range(2)]
G = [[0.0], [0.0]]
r = [0.0, 0.0]
for a, c in [([0.0, 0.0], 1.0), ([1.0, 1.0], 3.0)]:
    f = psi(a)
    for i in range(2):
        G[i][0] += f[i] * c
        r[i] += f[i]
g = psi([0.1, 0.0])
y = (G[0][0] * g[0] + G[1][0] * g[1]) / (r[0] * g[0] + r[1] * g[1])
print(json.dumps({"read": round(y, 6), "divisor": [round(v, 6) for v in r]}))
